value.zh: 游雅 高閭 趙逸 胡叟 胡方回 張湛 段承根 闞駰 劉延明 趙柔 索敞 宋繇 江式
value.en: You Ya, Gao Lu, Zhao Yi, Hu Sou, Hu Fanghui, Zhang Zhan, Duan Chenggen, Kang Yin, Liu Yanming, Zhao Rou, Sou Chang, Song Yao, and Jiang Shi
value.literal: You Ya, Gao Lu, Zhao Yi, Hu Sou, Hu Fanghui, Zhang Zhan, Duan Chenggen, Kang Yin, Liu Yanming, Zhao Rou, Sou Chang, Song Yao, Jiang Shi

value.zh: 魏初，博士清河張揖著《埤倉》、《廣雅》、《古今字詁》。
value.en: Early in Wei, Erudite Zhang Yi of Qinghe composed the Etymological Storehouse, the Broad Lexicon, and the Glosses on Ancient and Modern Characters.
value.literal: At the beginning of Wei, Erudite Zhang Yi of Qinghe wrote the *Etymological Storehouse*, the *Broad Lexicon*, and the *Glosses on Ancient and Modern Characters*.

value.zh: 究諸《埤》、《廣》，綴拾遺漏，增長事類，抑亦于文為益者。
value.en: In compiling the Storehouse and the Lexicon, he patched omissions and expanded the categories of terms—work that did some service to written learning.
value.literal: Examining the *Storehouse* and the *Lexicon*, patching omissions and adding categories of things, this too was of some benefit to letters.

value.zh: 然其《字詁》，方之許篇，古今體用，或得或失。
value.en: Yet in his Character Glosses, measured against Xu's treatise, the ancient and modern forms and usages were sometimes correct and sometimes mistaken.
value.literal: Yet in his *Character Glosses*, compared with Xu's work, the ancient and modern forms and usages were sometimes right and sometimes wrong.

value.zh: 陳留邯鄲淳亦與揖同，博開古藝，特善《倉》、《雅》。
value.en: Handan Chun of Chenliu was Zhang Yi's peer: broadly versed in ancient arts and especially masterful in the Cangjie and the Lexicon.
value.literal: Handan Chun of Chenliu was Zhang Yi's equal, broadly versed in ancient arts and especially skilled in the *Cangjie* and the *Lexicon*.

value.zh: 許氏字指、八體、六書，精究閑理，有名於揖。
value.en: In the Xu family's explanations of character purpose, the eight scripts, and the six principles, he pursued the subtle logic to the full and outshone Zhang Yi in reputation.
value.literal: In the Xu family's explanations of character purpose, the eight scripts, and the six principles, he thoroughly investigated subtle principles and was more renowned than Zhang Yi.

value.zh: 以書教諸皇子。
value.en: He instructed the princes in writing.
value.literal: He taught writing to the various princes.

value.zh: 又建《三字石經》於漢碑西，其文蔚煥，三體復宣。
value.en: He also set up the Three-Script Stone Classic west of the Han stele; its text shone with brilliance, and the three scripts were displayed once more.
value.literal: He also erected the *Three-Script Stone Classic* west of the Han stele; its text was splendidly luminous, and the three scripts were again displayed.

value.zh: 校之《說文》，篆、隸大同，而古字少異。
value.en: Checked against the Explaining Graphs, the seal and clerical forms were largely identical, though a few ancient characters differed.
value.literal: Compared with the *Explaining Graphs*, the seal and clerical forms were largely the same, though the ancient characters differed slightly.

value.zh: 又有京兆韋誕、河東衛覬二家，並號能篆。
value.en: Two other masters were famed for seal script: Wei Dan of Jingzhao and Wei Ji of Hedong.
value.literal: There were also two masters styled able in seal script: Wei Dan of Jingzhao and Wei Ji of Hedong.

value.zh: 當時台觀榜題，寶器之銘，悉是誕書。
value.en: In those days the inscriptions on palace towers and precious vessels were all written by Dan.
value.literal: At the time the inscriptions on palace towers and the texts on precious vessels were all in Dan's hand.

value.zh: 咸傳之子孫，世稱其妙。
value.en: Their art passed to their descendants, and for generations their skill was hailed as exquisite.
value.literal: All were handed down to their descendants, and generation after generation their skill was praised as marvelous.

value.zh: 晉世義陽王典祠令任城呂忱表上《字林》六卷，尋其況趣，附托許慎《說文》，而按偶章句，隱別古籀奇惑之字，文得正隸，不差篆意也。
value.en: In Jin, Lü Chen of Rencheng, director of sacrifices under the Prince of Yiyang, submitted the six scrolls of the Forest of Characters. In spirit it followed Xu Shen's Explaining Graphs, arranged entries in parallel phrases, and discreetly sorted out ancient Zhou forms, odd characters, and misleading variants, preserving correct clerical writing without abandoning seal-script meaning.
value.literal: In Jin, Lü Chen of Rencheng, Director of Sacrifices under the Prince of Yiyang, memorialized and submitted the six scrolls of the *Forest of Characters*; tracing its intent, it leaned on Xu Shen's *Explaining Graphs*, arranged parallel phrases, and discreetly distinguished ancient Zhou, odd, and misleading characters, so that the text kept correct clerical forms without losing seal intent.

value.zh: 忱弟靜別放故左校令李登《聲類》之法，作《韻集》五卷，使宮、商、角、徵、羽各為一篇，而文字與兄便是魯、衛，音讀楚、夏，時有不同。
value.en: Chen's younger brother Jing, adapting the method of Li Deng's Categories of Sounds, compiled the five scrolls of the Collection of Rhymes, with gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu each forming one chapter. In script he and his brother were as close as Lu to Wei, yet in pronunciation they were as far apart as Chu from Xia—sometimes they did not agree.
value.literal: Chen's younger brother Jing, separately following the method of the former Colonel Director of Works Li Deng's *Categories of Sounds*, composed the five scrolls of the *Collection of Rhymes*, making gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu each one chapter; yet in written characters he and his elder brother were like Lu and Wei, and in pronunciation Chu and Xia—at times they differed.

value.zh: 皇魏承百王之季，紹五運之緒。
value.en: Great Wei succeeded the last of the hundred kings and carried forward the line of the five cycles.
value.literal: Great Wei succeeded the last of the hundred kings and continued the thread of the five cycles.

value.zh: 世易風移，文字改變，篆形謬錯，隸體失真。
value.en: As times changed and customs shifted, the script altered too: seal forms grew corrupt and clerical writing lost its integrity.
value.literal: As the age changed and customs shifted, writing altered; seal forms went awry and clerical bodies lost their truth.

value.zh: 俗學鄙習，復加虛造。
value.en: Shallow scholarship and vulgar habit piled invention upon invention.
value.literal: Vulgar learning and base habit further added fictitious invention.

value.zh: 巧談辯士，以意為疑，炫惑于時，難以厘改。
value.en: Clever talkers and debaters, treating private fancy as grounds for doubt, dazzled their contemporaries and made correction nearly impossible.
value.literal: Clever talkers and debaters, taking their own whims as grounds for doubt, dazzled and misled the age, and correction was hard to achieve.

value.zh: 乃曰：追來為歸，巧言為辯，小免為< 需免>，神嵒為蠶。
value.en: They would say that zhui (follow) stood for gui (return), qiaoyan (clever speech) for bian (debate), xiaomian (small hare) for xumian, and shenyan (divine cliff) for can (silkworm).
value.literal: They would say: "follow" was written for "return," "clever speech" for "debate," "small hare" for "need hare," and "divine cliff" for "silkworm."

value.zh: 如斯甚眾，皆不合孔氏古書、史籀《大篆》、許氏《說文》、《石經》三字也。
value.en: Such cases were legion, and none accorded with the Kong family's ancient texts, Scribe Zhou's Great Seal, Xu Shen's Explaining Graphs, or the three-script stone classic.
value.literal: Cases like these were extremely numerous, and none accorded with the Kong family's ancient books, Scribe Zhou's *Great Seal*, Xu Shen's *Explaining Graphs*, or the three-script stone classic.

value.zh: 凡所關古，莫不惆悵焉。
value.en: Every matter touching the ancient script filled the heart with sorrow.
value.literal: Everything touching antiquity filled one with sorrow.

value.zh: 嗟夫！
value.en: Alas!
value.literal: Alas!

value.zh: 文字者六籍之宗，王教之始，前人所以垂今，今人所以識古。
value.en: Writing is the root of the Six Classics and the beginning of royal instruction: through it the ancients handed down the past to the present, and the present learns to know antiquity.
value.literal: Writing is the ancestor of the Six Classics and the beginning of royal teaching; by it the men of old handed down to the present, and the men of today recognize antiquity.

value.zh: 儒林上
value.en: Confucian Scholars, Part 1
value.literal: Confucian Forest, Upper

value.zh: 孫惠蔚，武邑武遂人也。
value.en: Sun Huiwei was from Wusui in Wuyi.
value.literal: Sun Huiwei was a man of Wusui in Wuyi.

value.zh: 年十五，粗通《詩》、《書》及《孝經》、《論語》。
value.en: At fifteen he had roughly mastered the Odes, Documents, Classic of Filial Piety, and Analects.
value.literal: At fifteen he roughly mastered the Odes, Documents, Classic of Filial Piety, and Analects.

value.zh: 十八，師董道季講《易》。
value.en: At eighteen he studied the Changes under Dong Daoji.
value.literal: At eighteen he studied the Changes under Dong Daoji.

value.zh: 十九，師程玄讀《禮經》及《春秋三傳》。
value.en: At nineteen he studied the Rites and the three Spring and Autumn commentaries under Cheng Xuan.
value.literal: At nineteen he studied the Book of Rites and the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn under Cheng Xuan.

value.zh: 周流儒肆，有名于冀方。
value.en: He traveled among Confucian schools and was renowned in Ji.
value.literal: He traveled through Confucian academies and was famous in the Ji region.

value.zh: 太和初，郡舉孝廉，對策於中書省。
value.en: In early Taihe his commandery recommended him as filial and incorrupt; he took the policy examination at the Secretariat.
value.literal: In early Taihe his commandery recommended him as filial and incorrupt; he answered policy questions at the Directorate of Archives.

value.zh: 時中書監高閭因相談薦，俄為中書博士，轉皇宗博士。
value.en: Director Gao Lu recommended him after conversation; he soon became Secretariat Doctor, then Imperial Clan Doctor.
value.literal: At that time Director Gao Lu because of conversation recommended him; soon he became Secretariat Doctor and was transferred to Imperial Clan Doctor.

value.zh: 閭被敕理定雅樂，惠蔚參其事。
value.en: Lu was ordered to arrange court music; Huiwei assisted.
value.literal: Lu received an edict to arrange the elegant music; Huiwei participated in the affair.

value.zh: 及樂成，閭上疏請集朝士于太樂，共研是非。
value.en: When the music was finished, Lu asked court gentlemen to review it at the Grand Music Office.
value.literal: When the music was completed, Lu submitted a memorial requesting court gentlemen assemble at the Grand Music Office to jointly investigate right and wrong.

value.zh: 秘書令李彪，自以才辯，立難於其前。
value.en: Secretariat Director Li Biao, confident in his eloquence, challenged him.
value.literal: Secretariat Director Li Biao, confident in his talent and eloquence, raised difficulties before him.

value.zh: 閭命惠蔚與彪抗論，彪不能屈。
value.en: Lu had Huiwei debate Biao, who could not prevail.
value.literal: Lu ordered Huiwei to debate with Biao; Biao could not overcome him.

value.zh: 黃門侍郎張彝，常與遊處，每表疏論事，多參訪焉。
value.en: Yellow Gate Gentleman Zhang Yi often consulted him on memorials.
value.literal: Yellow Gate Gentleman Zhang Yi often associated with him; whenever memorials discussed affairs, he often consulted him.

value.zh: 十七年，孝文南征，上議告類之禮。
value.en: In year seventeen, during Emperor Xiaowen's southern campaign, he memorialized on reporting rites to ancestors.
value.literal: In the seventeenth year, when Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south, he submitted a memorial on the ceremony of reporting to the ancestors.

value.zh: 及太師馮熙薨，惠蔚監其喪禮。
value.en: When Grand Tutor Feng Xi died, Huiwei supervised the mourning rites.
value.literal: When Grand Tutor Feng Xi died, Huiwei supervised his mourning rites.

value.zh: 上書，令熙未冠之子，皆服成人服。
value.en: He memorialized that Xi's uncapped sons should wear adult mourning.
value.literal: He submitted a memorial that Xi's sons who had not yet capped should all wear adult mourning garments.

value.zh: 惠蔚與李彪以儒學相知，及彪位至尚書，惠蔚仍太廟令。
value.en: Huiwei and Li Biao were friends in scholarship; when Biao became Minister, Huiwei remained Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
value.literal: Huiwei and Li Biao knew each other through Confucian learning; when Biao reached Minister, Huiwei remained Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

value.zh: 孝文曾從容言曰：「道固既登龍門，而孫蔚猶沈涓澮，朕常以為負矣。」
value.en: Emperor Xiaowen once said: "Dao Gu has crossed the Dragon Gate while Sun Wei remains in the mud—I have always regretted this."
value.literal: Emperor Xiaowen once said at leisure: "Dao Gu has ascended the Dragon Gate while Sun Wei still sinks in a muddy ford—I have always felt this a burden."

value.zh: 雖久滯小官，深體通塞，無孜孜之望，儒者以是尚焉。
value.en: Though long in minor posts, he understood fortune and setback without ambition; scholars esteemed him.
value.literal: Though long stuck in minor office, he deeply understood fortune and obstruction and had no eager hopes; Confucians therefore esteemed him.

value.zh: 二十二年，侍讀東宮。
value.en: In year twenty-two he lectured in the Eastern Palace.
value.literal: In the twenty-second year he served as lecturer in the Eastern Palace.

value.zh: 先是，七廟以平文為太祖。
value.en: Earlier the seven temples took Emperor Pingwen as Founder.
value.literal: Earlier the seven temples took Emperor Pingwen as Founder.

value.zh: 孝文議定祖宗，以道武為太祖。
value.en: Emperor Xiaowen fixed Emperor Daowu as Founder.
value.literal: Emperor Xiaowen deliberated fixing the ancestors and took Emperor Daowu as Founder.

value.zh: 祖宗雖定，然昭穆未改。
value.en: Though ancestors were fixed, the zhao-mu order was unchanged.
value.literal: Though the ancestors were fixed, the zhao and mu order was not yet changed.

value.zh: 及孝文崩，將祔神主於廟。
value.en: When Emperor Xiaowen died, spirit tablets were to be installed in the temple.
value.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen died, spirit tablets were to be enshrined in the temple.

value.zh: 侍中崔光兼太常卿，以太祖既改，昭穆以次而易。
value.en: Cui Guang, also Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, held that with the Founder changed, zhao-mu should shift accordingly.
value.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang, also Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, held that since the Founder was changed, zhao and mu should change in sequence accordingly.

value.zh: 兼御史中尉、黃門侍郎邢巒，以為太祖雖改，昭穆仍不應易，乃立彈草，欲按奏光。
value.en: Xing Luan held that zhao-mu should not change despite the new Founder and drafted impeachment against Guang.
value.literal: Concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Yellow Gate Gentleman Xing Luan held that though the Founder was changed, zhao and mu still should not change; he drafted an impeachment to report Guang.

value.zh: 光謂惠蔚曰：「此乃禮也，而執法欲見彈劾，思獲助於碩學。」
value.en: Guang told Huiwei: "This is ritual, yet legal officers wish to impeach me—I need your help."
value.literal: Guang told Huiwei: "This is ritual law, yet the law officers wish to impeach me—I seek help from a great scholar."

value.zh: 惠蔚曰：「此深得禮變。」
value.en: Huiwei said: "This accords with proper ritual change."
value.literal: Huiwei said: "This deeply obtains the ritual change."

value.zh: 尋為書以與光，贊明其事。
value.en: He soon wrote supporting Guang's position.
value.literal: Soon he wrote a letter for Guang clarifying the matter.

value.zh: 光以惠蔚書呈宰輔，乃召惠蔚與巒庭議得失。
value.en: Guang presented the letter and summoned Huiwei and Luan to debate at court.
value.literal: Guang presented Huiwei's letter to the chief ministers and summoned Huiwei and Luan to court to debate gains and losses.

value.zh: 尚書令王肅又助巒，而巒理終屈，彈事遂寢。
value.en: Minister Wang Su aided Luan, but Luan lost the debate and the impeachment was dropped.
value.literal: Minister Wang Su again aided Luan, but Luan's reasoning was ultimately defeated and the impeachment was shelved.

value.zh: 孝武皇帝，景帝中子也，母曰王美人。
value.en: Emperor Wu was Emperor Jing's middle son. His mother was Lady Wang, a royal beauty.
value.literal: Filial Martial Emperor, Emperor Jing's middle son; his mother was called Lady Wang, the Beauty.

value.zh: 年四歲立為膠東王。
value.en: At age four, he was made King of Jiaodong.
value.literal: Age four years established as Jiaodong King.

value.zh: 七歲為皇太子，母為皇后。
value.en: At age seven, he became crown prince, and his mother was made empress.
value.literal: Seven years old became Crown Prince, mother became Empress.

value.zh: 十六歲，後三年正月，景帝崩。
value.en: At age sixteen, in the first month of the third year of Houyuan, Emperor Jing passed away.
value.literal: Sixteen years old, in the first month of the third year of Houyuan, Emperor Jing passed away.

value.zh: 甲子，太子即皇帝位，尊皇太后竇氏曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。
value.en: On the jiazi day, the crown prince ascended the throne as emperor. He honored Empress Dowager Dou as Grand Empress Dowager and the empress as Empress Dowager.
value.literal: Jiazi day, Crown Prince ascended emperor position, honored Empress Dowager Dou clan as Grand Empress Dowager, Empress as Empress Dowager.

value.zh: 三月，封皇太后同母弟田蚡、勝皆為列侯。
value.en: In the third month, he enfeoffed the Empress Dowager's uterine brothers Tian Fen and Sheng as marquises.
value.literal: Third month, enfeoffed Empress Dowager same-mother younger brothers Tian Fen, Sheng all as marquises.

value.zh: 建元元年冬十月，詔丞相、御史、列侯、中二千石、二千石、諸侯相舉賢良方正直言極諫之士。
value.en: In winter, in the tenth month of the first year of Jianyuan, an edict ordered the Chancellor, the Imperial Secretary, the marquises, senior court officials, and the chancellors of the feudal states to recommend men of worth and integrity who could speak frankly and remonstrate without reserve.
value.literal: In winter, in the tenth month of the first year of Jianyuan, an edict ordered the Chancellor, the Imperial Secretary, the listed marquises, officials of the middle two-thousand-bushel rank, officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank, and the chancellors of the feudal states to recommend men who were worthy and good, upright and forthright, and able to speak directly and remonstrate to the utmost.

value.zh: 丞相綰奏：「所舉賢良，或治申、商、韓非、蘇秦、張儀之言，亂國政，請皆罷。」
value.en: Chancellor Wan memorialized: "Some of the men recommended for worth study Shen Buhai, Shang Yang, Han Fei, Su Qin, and Zhang Yi, doctrines that disorder state government. I request that they all be dismissed."
value.literal: Chancellor Wan memorialized: "Among those recommended as worthy and good, some study the teachings of Shen, Shang, Han Fei, Su Qin, and Zhang Yi, which disorder the government of the state; I request that all be dismissed."

value.zh: 奏可。
value.en: The memorial was approved.
value.literal: The memorial was approved.

value.zh: 卷六十二 司馬遷傳第三十二
value.en: Volume 62: Biography 32—Sima Qian.
value.literal: Volume 62: Biographies the Thirty-second, Sima Qian.

value.zh: 自司馬氏去周適晉，分散，或在衛，或在趙，或在秦。
value.en: After the Simas left Zhou for Jin the line split among Wei, Zhao, and Qin.
value.literal: From the time the Sima clan left Zhou for Jin, they scattered; some were in Wei, some in Zhao, some in Qin.

value.zh: 其在衛者，相中山。
value.en: The Wei branch produced a chancellor of Zhongshan.
value.literal: Those who were in Wei became chancellor of Zhongshan.

value.zh: 在趙者，以傳劍論顯，蒯聵其後也。
value.en: The Zhao line rose on fencing theory; Kuai Kui was of that stock.
value.literal: Those in Zhao became eminent through treatises on sword transmission; Kuai Kui was their descendant.

value.zh: 在秦者錯，與張儀爭論，於是惠王使錯將兵伐蜀，遂拔，因而守之。
value.en: In Qin, Cuo crossed swords in debate with Zhang Yi; King Hui sent him to conquer Shu, which he held thereafter.
value.literal: The one in Qin was Cuo; he debated with Zhang Yi; thereupon King Hui sent Cuo to lead troops to attack Shu, then took it, and thereupon guarded it.

value.zh: 錯孫蘄，事武安君白起。
value.en: Cuo's grandson Qi served Lord Wu'an, Bai Qi.
value.literal: Cuo's grandson was Qi; he served Lord Wu'an Bai Qi.

value.zh: 而少梁更名夏陽。
value.en: Shaoliang was later renamed Xiayang.
value.literal: And Shaoliang was renamed Xiayang.

value.zh: 蘄與武安君坑趙長平軍，還而與之俱賜死杜郵，葬於華池。
value.en: Qi helped Bai Qi slaughter the Zhao army at Changping; on the march home both were ordered to commit suicide at Duyou and were buried at Huachi.
value.literal: Qi together with Lord Wu'an buried alive Zhao's army at Changping; returning, together with him he was ordered to die at Duyou and was buried at Huachi.

value.zh: 蘄孫昌，為秦王鐵官。
value.en: Qi's grandson Chang ran the royal foundries for the king of Qin.
value.literal: Qi's grandson was Chang; he was Qin's king's ironworks officer.

value.zh: 當始皇之時，蒯聵玄孫卬為武信君將而徇朝歌。
value.en: Under the First Emperor, Ang—fourth-generation descendant of Kuai Kui—served Lord Wuxin as a general and reduced Zhaoge.
value.literal: In First Emperor's time Kuai Kui's great-great-grandson Ang was general under Lord Wuxin and campaigned to Zhaoge.

value.zh: 諸侯之相王，王卬於殷。
value.en: When the lords began proclaiming kings, Ang was enthroned in the Yin region.
value.literal: When the feudal lords set one another up as kings, they made Ang king in Yin.

value.zh: 漢之伐楚，卬歸漢，以其地為河內郡。
value.en: When Han struck Chu, Ang came over, and his lands were organized as Henei commandery.
value.literal: In Han's attack on Chu, Ang submitted to Han; his territory became Henei commandery.

value.zh: 昌生毋懌，毋懌為漢市長。
value.en: Chang's son Wu Yi became market commissioner under Han.
value.literal: Chang begat Wu Yi; Wu Yi was Han's market chief.

value.zh: 毋懌生喜，喜為五大夫，卒，皆葬高門。
value.en: Wu Yi's son Xi held fifth-rank grandee rank; father and son lie buried at Gaomen.
value.literal: Wu Yi begat Xi; Xi was a fifth-rank grandee; when he died, both were buried at Gaomen.

value.zh: 喜生談，談為太史公。
value.en: Xi fathered Tan, who became grand scribe.
value.literal: Xi begat Tan; Tan was the grand scribe.

value.zh: 徒單兀典
value.en: Tudan Wudian
value.literal: Tudan Wudian

value.zh: 天興元年正月，朝廷聞大兵入饒風，移兀典行省閿鄉，以備潼關。
value.en: In the first month of Tianxing 1 (1232), the court learned that the Mongol army had entered Raofeng. Wudian's provincial headquarters was transferred to Minxiang to prepare the defense of Tong Pass.
value.literal: In the first month of the first year of Tianxing, the court heard that the great army had entered Raofeng; Wudian's provincial headquarters was moved to Minxiang to prepare the defense of Tong Pass.

value.zh: 徒單百家為關陝總帥，便宜行事。
value.en: Tudan Baijia was appointed overall commander of the Guan-Shaan region with discretionary authority.
value.literal: Tudan Baijia was made overall commander of Guan and Shaan, with discretionary authority.

value.zh: 百家馳入陝，榜州民雲：「淮南透漏軍馬，慮其道由潼關，勢不能守，縣鎮遷入大城，糧斛輜重聚之陝州，近山者入山寨避兵。」
value.en: Baijia rode posthaste into Shaanzhou and posted a notice to the people: "Enemy forces have broken through from Huainan. Fearing they may advance by way of Tong Pass, we cannot hold this position. Move from the county towns into the major cities; concentrate grain and baggage at Shaanzhou; those near the mountains should take refuge in stockaded strongholds."
value.literal: Baijia galloped into Shaan and posted a notice to the prefectural populace, saying: "Enemy forces have leaked through from Huainan; fearing they may come by way of Tong Pass, the position cannot be held. County towns are to move into the great cities; grain and baggage are to be gathered at Shaanzhou; those near the mountains are to enter stockaded strongholds to avoid the troops."

value.zh: 會阿裏合傳旨召兀典入援，兀典遂與潼關總帥納合合閏、秦藍總帥都點檢完顏重喜、安平都尉苗秀、蕩寇都尉術甲某、振武都尉張翼及虎威、鷹揚、葭州劉趙二帥，軍十有一萬、騎五千，盡撒秦藍諸隘之備。
value.en: Just then Aliha relayed an imperial order summoning Wudian to reinforce the capital. Wudian assembled Tong Pass commander-in-chief Nahan Hehun, Qin-Lan overall commander and chief inspector Wanyan Chongxi, commandants Miao Xiu of Anping, Shujia Mou of Bandit-Suppression, and Zhang Yi of Zhenwu, along with the Tiger Might, Eagle Soar, and the Liu and Zhao commanders of Jia Prefecture—eleven thousand foot soldiers and five thousand horsemen—and stripped all the pass defenses in Qin and Lan.
value.literal: It happened that Aliha transmitted an edict summoning Wudian to reinforce the capital. Wudian then joined with Tong Pass commander-in-chief Nahan Hehun, Qin-Lan overall commander and chief inspector Wanyan Chongxi, Anping commandant Miao Xiu, Bandit-Suppression commandant Shujia Mou, Zhenwu commandant Zhang Yi, and the Tiger Might, Eagle Soar, and the two commanders Liu and Zhao of Jia Prefecture—eleven thousand infantry and five thousand cavalry—and completely withdrew the defenses of all passes in Qin and Lan.

value.zh: 從虢入陝。
value.en: They entered Shaanzhou from Guo Prefecture.
value.literal: He entered Shaan from Guo.

value.zh: 同、華、閿鄉一帶軍糧數十萬斛，備關船二百餘艘，皆順流東下。
value.en: Several hundred thousand hu of military grain in the Tong, Hua, and Minxiang region, along with more than two hundred supply boats, were all sent downstream to the east.
value.literal: In the Tong, Hua, and Minxiang region military grain amounted to several hundred thousand hu; more than two hundred pass-defense boats were prepared—all went downstream to the east.

value.zh: 俄聞大兵近，糧皆不及載，船悉空下。
value.en: Soon word came that the Mongol army was near. There was no time to load the grain, and the boats sailed downstream empty.
value.literal: Shortly they heard the great army was near; the grain could not all be loaded in time, and the boats all went down empty.

value.zh: 複盡起州民，連靈寶、硤石倉粟，遊騎至，殺掠不勝計。
value.en: They mobilized the entire prefectural population and emptied the granaries of Lingbao and Xiaoshi as well. When Mongol scouting parties arrived, the killing and plundering were beyond reckoning.
value.literal: They again mobilized all the prefectural populace, linking the granaries of Lingbao and Xiaoshi; when roaming cavalry arrived, the killing and plundering were beyond counting.

value.zh: 又遣陝州觀察副使兼規措轉運副使抹撚速也以船八十往運潼關、閿鄉糧，行及靈寶北河夾灘。
value.en: They also sent Shaanzhou assistant surveillance commissioner and concurrent assistant transport commissioner Mo'nian Suoye with eighty boats to transport grain from Tong Pass and Minxiang. The convoy reached the narrows of the northern river at Lingbao.
value.literal: They also dispatched Shaanzhou assistant surveillance commissioner and concurrent assistant transport planning commissioner Mo'nian Suoye with eighty boats to transport grain from Tong Pass and Minxiang; they reached the narrows of the northern river at Lingbao.

value.zh: 義軍張信、侯三集壯士三百余，保老幼，立水柵。
value.en: Volunteer commanders Zhang Xin and Hou San rallied more than three hundred stalwarts to protect the elderly and children and erected a water barrier.
value.literal: Volunteer forces Zhang Xin and Hou San gathered more than three hundred stalwarts, protected the old and young, and erected a water barrier.

value.zh: 北將忽魯罕只乘淺攻之不能克，遇速也船至即降，大兵得此船遂破侯、張，殺戮殆盡。
value.en: The Mongol general Huluhazi attacked at the shallows but could not break through. When Suoye's boats arrived he surrendered immediately. The Mongols seized those boats, overran Hou and Zhang's force, and slaughtered nearly everyone.
value.literal: The northern general Huluhazi attacked at the shallows but could not overcome them. When Suoye's boats arrived he surrendered at once; the great army obtained these boats and then broke Hou and Zhang, slaughtering nearly all.

value.zh: 初，兀典發閿鄉，拜天，賞軍，人白金三兩，將校有差。
value.en: When Wudian first set out from Minxiang, he worshipped Heaven and rewarded the troops—three taels of silver per soldier, with graded amounts for officers.
value.literal: At the outset, when Wudian set out from Minxiang, he worshipped Heaven and rewarded the army—three taels of silver per man, with differences for officers.

value.zh: 州之庫藏，軍資器械，為之一空。
value.en: The prefectural treasuries and all military stores and equipment were emptied.
value.literal: The prefecture's treasuries and military stores and equipment were emptied by this.

value.zh: 期日進發，已而不行，日造銀器及兵幕牌印，陝州及鹽司牌亦奪取之。
value.en: A departure date was set, yet they did not march. Day after day Wudian had silver vessels, military tent plaques, and seals manufactured, and he seized the official plaques of Shaanzhou and the Salt Commission as well.
value.literal: A day was set for advance, yet afterward they did not move; day by day silver vessels and military tent plaques and seals were made, and the plaques of Shaanzhou and the Salt Commission were also seized.

value.zh: 又欲卻州民財物以資軍，素蘭諫之而止。
value.en: He also planned to seize civilian property to fund the army, but Sulan's remonstrance put a stop to it.
value.literal: He also wished to take back the populace's goods and property to supply the army; Sulan remonstrated and it was stopped.

value.zh: 二月戊午，乃行。
value.en: On the wuwu day of the second month they finally set out.
value.literal: On the wuwu day of the second month, they finally marched.

value.zh: 有李先生者諫曰：「方今大兵俱在河南，河北空虛，相公可先取衛州，出其不意。
value.en: A certain Master Li remonstrated: "The Mongol army is now entirely in Henan, and Hebei lies empty. Your Excellency could seize Weizhou first and take them by surprise.
value.literal: A certain Master Li remonstrated, saying: "At present the great army is all in Henan; Hebei is empty. Your Excellency could first take Weizhou by surprise.

value.zh: 彼知我軍在北，必分兵北渡，京師即得少寬，相公入援亦易為矣。」
value.en: Once they learn our army is in the north, they will have to divide their forces to cross the river, giving the capital some breathing room and making your relief march far easier."
value.literal: When they know our army is in the north, they will certainly divide forces to cross north; the capital will gain some relief, and Your Excellency's relief mission will also be easier."

value.zh: 兀典大怒，以為泄軍機，斬之於市，遂行。
value.en: Wudian flew into a rage, accused him of leaking military secrets, and had him executed in the marketplace before marching on.
value.literal: Wudian was greatly enraged, believing he had leaked military secrets, and executed him in the marketplace; then they marched.

value.zh: 軍士各以老幼自隨。
value.en: Every soldier brought his elderly dependents and children along.
value.literal: Each soldier brought old and young dependents along.

value.zh: 州中亦有關中、河中遷避商賈老幼，亦倚兵力從行，婦女皆嫁士卒，軍中亦有強娶奪者。
value.en: Merchants and their families who had fled from Guanzhong and Hezhong also joined the column, trusting in military protection. Women were married off to soldiers, and some soldiers seized wives by force.
value.literal: In the prefecture there were also merchants and their old and young who had fled from Guanzhong and Hezhong; they too relied on military strength to go along. Women were all given in marriage to soldiers, and in the army there were also those who seized wives by force.

value.zh: 是日，軍出兩東門及南門，不遵洛陽路，乃由州西南徑入大山冰雪中。
value.en: That day the army marched out through both eastern gates and the southern gate, avoiding the Luoyang road and plunging southwest from the prefecture straight into snowbound mountains.
value.literal: That day the army went out through both eastern gates and the southern gate, not following the Luoyang road but entering directly into the great mountains and snow and ice by way of the prefecture's southwest.

value.zh: 葭州劉、趙兩帥即日叛去，大兵以數百騎遙躡其後。
value.en: The Liu and Zhao commanders of Jia Prefecture defected that same day. Several hundred Mongol horsemen trailed the column at a distance.
value.literal: The Liu and Zhao commanders of Jia Prefecture defected that very day; the great army followed at a distance with several hundred horsemen.

value.zh: 明日，張翼軍叛往硃陽，入鹿盧關，大兵追及降之。
value.en: The next day Zhang Yi's force defected toward Zhuyang and entered Lulu Pass. The Mongols caught up and accepted their surrender.
value.literal: The next day Zhang Yi's army defected toward Zhuyang, entered Lulu Pass, and when the great army caught up they surrendered.

value.zh: 山路積雪，晝日凍釋，泥淖及脛，隨軍婦女棄擲幼稚，哀號盈路。
value.en: Snow lay deep on the mountain paths. By day it thawed and refroze, mud reaching to the shins. Women in the column abandoned their infants, and wailing filled the road.
value.literal: Snow lay deep on the mountain road; by day it thawed and froze again, mud reaching to the shins. Women following the army abandoned infants; wailing filled the road.

value.zh: 軍至鐵嶺，大兵潛召洛陽大軍從西三縣過盧氏，所至燒官民廬舍積聚，慮為金軍所據，又反守鐵嶺，以斷歸路。
value.en: When the Jin army reached Tieling, the Mongols secretly summoned their Luoyang forces through the three western counties via Lushi. Wherever they went they burned official and civilian buildings and stores lest the Jin seize them, then turned back to hold Tieling and cut off the retreat.
value.literal: When the army reached Tieling, the great army secretly summoned the Luoyang forces to pass through the three western counties via Lushi; wherever they went they burned official and civilian dwellings and stores, fearing the Jin army would seize them; they also turned back to hold Tieling and cut off the route of retreat.

value.zh: 金兵知必死，皆有鬥志，然已數日不食，行二百里許，困憊不支，頗亦散走。
value.en: The Jin soldiers knew they faced certain death and fought with desperate resolve, but they had not eaten for days. After marching some two hundred li they collapsed from exhaustion, and many scattered in flight.
value.literal: The Jin troops knew they must die and all had fighting spirit, yet they had not eaten for several days; after marching some two hundred li they were exhausted beyond endurance and many also scattered and fled.

value.zh: 於是完顏重喜先降，大軍斬于馬前。
value.en: Wanyan Chongxi was the first to surrender, and the Mongols beheaded him before their horses.
value.literal: Thereupon Wanyan Chongxi surrendered first, and the great army beheaded him before their horses.
